focus.title: 美欧拟对华电动汽车加征新关税，中企应提前布局供应链合规
focus.summary: 据多方消息，美国与欧盟正酝酿于2026年第四季度对进口自中国的电动汽车及关键零部件加征新一轮关税，税率或分别升至35%和30%。此举将显著提高中国车企出口成本，并可能引发连锁反制。建议相关企业立即审查原产地规则与供应链布局，考虑在东南亚或墨西哥设立组装环节以规避关税，同时做好应对欧盟碳边境调节机制（CBAM）的合规准备。
focus.source: 来源：综合路透社、彭博社报道 · 2026.08.25
focus.title_en: US and EU Plan New Tariffs on Chinese EVs; Chinese Firms Urged to Rethink Supply Chains
focus.summary_en: Multiple sources indicate that the US and EU are preparing to impose new tariffs of up to 35% and 30%, respectively, on Chinese-made electric vehicles and key components in Q4 2026. This will significantly raise export costs and may trigger retaliatory measures. Companies are advised to review rules of origin and supply chain strategies, consider assembly operations in Southeast Asia or Mexico, and prepare for the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).
focus.source_en: Source: Compiled from Reuters and Bloomberg reports · 2026.08.25

case.title: 新加坡国际仲裁中心裁决获中国法院承认，明确仲裁条款独立性原则
case.summary: 2026年8月，广东省深圳市中级人民法院裁定承认并执行新加坡国际仲裁中心（SIAC）作出的一项涉外商事仲裁裁决。该案中，被申请人主张主合同无效导致仲裁条款失效，但法院依据《纽约公约》及中国仲裁法，强调仲裁条款独立于主合同，主合同效力争议不影响仲裁协议的效力，最终支持了申请人的执行请求。此案为中国企业参与国际仲裁提供了积极信号，提示企业在起草合同时应明确约定仲裁条款的独立性。
case.source: 来源：广东省高级人民法院官网案例发布 · 2026.08
case.title_en: Chinese Court Recognizes SIAC Award, Upholding Principle of Arbitration Clause Autonomy
case.summary_en: In August 2026, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court in Guangdong Province ruled to recognize and enforce an international commercial arbitration award rendered by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC). The respondent argued that the invalidity of the main contract nullified the arbitration clause, but the court, citing the New York Convention and Chinese arbitration law, held that the arbitration clause is independent of the main contract, and disputes over the latter's validity do not affect the former. This ruling signals a favorable attitude towards international arbitration and reminds Chinese enterprises to explicitly provide for the autonomy of arbitration clauses in contracts.
case.source_en: Source: Case published on official website of Guangdong High People's Court · 2026.08

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区跨境数据流动新规出台，便利企业合规开展国际业务
policy.summary: 2026年8月20日，国家网信办联合广东省等部门发布《粤港澳大湾区数据跨境流动安全管理规范（试行）》，自2026年10月1日起实施。新规明确在大湾区内试行数据跨境流动“白名单”制度，对列入清单的常见商业数据（如贸易、物流、支付信息）简化安全评估流程，同时强化重要数据和个人信息保护。此举将降低企业跨境数据传输的合规成本，鼓励大湾区企业利用香港、澳门平台拓展国际市场。
policy.source: 来源：国家互联网信息办公室官网 · 2026.08.20
policy.title_en: New Cross-Border Data Flow Rules for Greater Bay Area Aim to Facilitate International Business
policy.summary_en: On August 20, 2026, the Cyberspace Administration of China, together with Guangdong Province and other departments, issued the 'Administrative Measures for Cross-Border Data Flow in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Trial)', effective October 1, 2026. The new rules introduce a 'whitelist' mechanism for cross-border data flows within the GBA, simplifying security assessments for common commercial data (e.g., trade, logistics, payment information) while strengthening protection of important data and personal information. This will reduce compliance costs for cross-border data transfers and encourage enterprises in the GBA to leverage Hong Kong and Macao platforms for global expansion.
policy.source_en: Source: Official website of Cyberspace Administration of China · 2026.08.20

analysis.title: 秦林蒿律师研判：美国出口管制新规下，中国企业应构建全流程合规体系
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师研判：近期美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）持续扩大对华实体清单管制范围，并强化对“最终用户”的审查。中企在涉美业务中面临更大的合规风险。建议企业：一是建立出口管制合规内控机制，对产品、客户、最终用途进行筛查；二是在合同中加入出口管制合规条款，明确双方责任；三是定期开展合规培训，并聘请专业律师进行风险评估。同时，利用中国商务部“不可靠实体清单”等反制工具，维护自身合法权益。
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin's View: Chinese Companies Should Build End-to-End Compliance Systems Amid US Export Controls
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's view: The US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has been expanding the Entity List and intensifying end-user checks. Chinese companies face growing compliance risks in US-related business. Recommendations: (1) establish internal export control compliance mechanisms to screen products, customers, and end-uses; (2) include export control compliance clauses in contracts to allocate responsibilities; (3) conduct regular compliance training and engage professional counsel for risk assessments. Meanwhile, use China's countermeasures, such as the 'Unreliable Entity List', to protect legitimate rights.
